posts.title: China, EU make progress on hybrid trade as EU says exports will be halved
posts.summary:
China said the understanding complies with WTO rules; the EU trade commissioner said it includes halving hybrid vehicle exports to the bloc.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China and the EU have reached a preliminary understanding to halve exports of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) and plug-in hybrids (PHEVs) to the European bloc.
The agreement also includes improved market access for EU companies in China and the easing of rare earth export licensing requirements.
While both sides claim the understanding complies with WTO rules, specific implementation timelines and mechanisms for the export reductions remain undisclosed.
This development serves as a critical first step in de-escalating trade tensions, with further negotiations scheduled to reconvene by January.

posts.title: China's September NEV wholesale sales estimated at 2026 high of 1.67 million, CPCA says
posts.summary:
Strong exports supported wholesale growth, while domestic retail sales remained under pressure.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China's passenger NEV wholesale sales reached an estimated 1.67 million units in September 2026, marking the highest monthly volume of the year.
Strong export performance served as the primary driver for wholesale growth, effectively offsetting weakness in domestic retail sales.
Year-to-date wholesale sales reached approximately 11.42 million units, representing a 10% increase compared to the same period in 2025.
BYD, Geely, and Chery led the market in September, with all top five manufacturers recording both year-on-year and month-on-month growth.

posts.title: We’re still figuring out the side effects of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs
posts.summary: This week my colleague Antonio Regalado had an interesting update on GLP-1 weight-loss drugs. According to research presented at an aging meeting in Boston, these drugs seem to affect at least some measures of biological age. Overweight and diabetic people who take GLP-1s have a biological age around two to three years younger than similar…
bullets: GLP-1 usage in the US has surged significantly, with 11% of Americans currently taking the drugs for weight loss compared to 3% in 2024.
New research suggests GLP-1 drugs may reduce biological age by two to three years in overweight or diabetic populations, expanding their perceived value beyond weight management.
Pharmaceutical manufacturers Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk are facing litigation over potential links between their drugs and rare cases of vision loss, though the scientific consensus remains mixed.
Beyond common gastrointestinal issues, ongoing research is evaluating the long-term impact of these drugs on hair, nails, and potential neurodegenerative or substance-use disorder treatments.

posts.title: The Download: AI’s refusal problem and weight-loss drug side effects
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. We’re putting too much faith in AI’s ability to say no Today’s AI models are trained to refuse a vast number of prompts. If you ask your chatbot how to poison…
bullets: AI models are increasingly engineered to refuse harmful prompts, yet these safety mechanisms are prone to failure and could be weaponized for state-level censorship.
The dual-use nature of AI creates a paradox where capabilities required for medical breakthroughs, such as cancer research, overlap with those needed to develop biological pathogens.
Emerging research indicates GLP-1 weight-loss drugs may slow biological aging, though clinicians are investigating potential side effects including hair loss, nail disorders, and optic nerve damage.
Envision Energy is scaling its climate tech operations by integrating wind power generation directly with on-site battery storage for data centers.

posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
$2B foundry pact; hyper-NA EUV; TSMC, Samsung financials; Canon readies nanoimprint; AI chips under scrutiny; $10T data center buildout; $1.5B SiC boost; chip smuggling; 800V power gains traction; quantum HW scales up; wireless EV road charging; sub-nm gate dielectrics; mobile fab.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: TSMC and GlobalFoundries have entered a $2 billion agreement to produce silicon interposers for CoWoS advanced packaging at the Malta, New York facility, with volume production slated for 2028.
Wolfspeed secured a $1.5 billion conditional commitment from the U.S. government to scale domestic production of silicon carbide materials and wide-bandgap power devices.
Global semiconductor sales surpassed $1 trillion year-to-date, with August monthly sales reaching $159.7 billion, representing an 8% increase over July figures.
McKinsey forecasts that AI inference will represent 60% of total AI compute demand by 2030, necessitating significant investments in custom accelerators, HBM, and silicon photonics.

Emerging AI-driven infrastructure startups, including Vinci and VEIR, raised significant capital to address critical bottlenecks in thermal simulation and superconducting power delivery for data centers.
